The Surgeon | Dr Patel

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
With numerous botched surgeries reported and even some deaths, we ask the question why is the surgeon responsible still allowed to practice.

Unique Selling Point:
We were approached by numerous ex-patients of Dr Soraya Patel about botched operations performed on them by the doctor and the devastating effect it has had on their physical and mental health.
The investigation also uncovered that in 5 years , the HPCSA has done nothing to stop the doctor after damning evidence was reported.

Summary:
The story of Soraya Patel starts in 2017 at the Glynwood Life hospital where she practiced as a general surgeon in Laparoscopic surgery. Within months fellow surgeons started to raise flags about her questionable practices. She would perform a routine Lap Nissen ( Hernia) operation for 11 hours. A procedure that normally takes between 27 - 45 minutes. Her patients would be gravely ill post-op an many spent up to a month in high care. It was suggested that she was put under supervision but she declined. She was barred from ever working at a Life Hospital again. She sued the 4 surgeons that reported her. The case was heard in the high court and the judge ruled in favour of the surgeons with cost.
She was then granted admission rights to the Netcare Sunward Park hospital. Surgeons at Sunward raised flags with the Hospital Manager Dr Annemarie Richter about Patel's ethical conduct. Despite that Dr Richter continued to give her admission rights to practice. To this day Netcare Group continues their support of Patel's admission rights. The Association of Surgeons was contacted for advice. The suggested peer review but she refused claiming that she was being bullied by a bunch of men. The HPCSA was approached. Patel started sending threatening letters to one of the concerned surgeons, she followed him home one evening and sat watching him from her vehicle when he entered his home. It left the doctor , traumatised and vulnerable. There were numerous reports from staff members who had been offered money. There were complaints from staff that she altered prescriptions - photos were taken by staff. Drains were incorrectly connected but Patel blamed staff. She also removed ICU files. Hospital security had to retrieve the files but some of them had already been altered. Patel also allowed her colleague Prof Ghoor to perform surgeries on patients without the patient knowledge or consent. The doctors also reported her disrespect for the Hypocratic Oath. We have obtained a list of patients deceased after Patel performed surgery. Eventually she was barred from practicing at any Netcare Facility in SA. Patel took legal action agains the doctors that reported her. They are unable and not willing to speak to CB as the case is still pending. Patel then gained admission rights from a private clinic in Kempton Park called Arwyp. She was given admission by the very same person that had her barred from Netcare - Zakeriah Esterhuizen. He moved from Sunward to Arwyp.
It is at Arwyp that she performed many questionable surgeries on our case studies.


Further information:
Arwyp is a privately owned hospital in Kempton Part.

But we got an opinion from a medical expert, who says this report is seriously questionable. V/O According to a doctor who examined Elzette months later - instead of a hernia repair, Dr Patel seems to have performed a gastric sleeve - which removes a section of the stomach. It’s a procedure usually performed to assist with weight loss. V/O Dr Patel says IF Elzette ever had a gastric sleeve operation, it must have been performed by another surgeon. She also insists that Elzette was kept in high care because of a bladder infection. Elzette I'm living on painkillers, like he has to force me to eat something. I drink two painkillers with my meal. Otherwise, I can’t sit, I can't lie, I can't stand. V/O Our expert believes Elzette should never have undergone surgery in the first place. And she will need further medical examination, to understand exactly what surgery she received under Dr Patel.. [PAUSE] V/O Assiem Alli is another of Dr Patel’s former patients. He underwent hernia repair surgery… twice. Assiem Went away home, started diet, ate all the liquids and soft stuff and all that in week past, two week past three weeks. But she had told me I can start having soft food like, mash and as I was eating, I was throwing up. Third week past. It was getting worse. VO ROR Asiem Dr Patel says, Asiem is responsible for his second emergency surgery, because he didn’t follow post-operative instructions. She says, he ate solid food, causing vomiting and severe damage to his repaired hernia, diaphragm and stomach. Link This referral for the second surgery makes no mention of an emergency or of the damage Dr Patel says was there. So what really went wrong after Assiem’s first surgery? V/O Questions and allegations against Dr Patel keep mounting. In Part 3 of our investigation, we demand answers. TEASER UPS from interview Claire: So in the meantime, with all these complaints she’s registered and still practising? Kwena: She is registered, and she is practising…. AD BREAK 2 PART 3 Intro Part 3 V/O Her name is Dr Soraya Patel – a surgeon specialising in laparoscopic and weight loss procedures. Over the past few months, numerous former patients have come forward with shocking stories of alleged malpractice… Hennie It’s very hard for me because I’m only 33. My life stopped, it’s damaged. It’s gone. V/O Hennie Like many other patients, Hennie van Staden suffered from acid reflux. After multiple operations with other doctors, he consulted Dr Patel, who performed a “redo” - and then two more “repairs” before the year was out. He spent weeks in high care. He alleges that the experience, and ongoing complications, have had a serious impact on his mental health. Hennie I take 3 to 4 sleeping pills a day just to sleep and get this pain away. And this feeling, this nonsense feels like things is living in my skin. VO ROR Hennie Dr Patel declined our request for an interview and opted to respond in writing. She claims that Hennie was responsible for the additional “redos” because he didn’t follow post-surgery instructions, and claims his mental health problems began BEFORE he came to her surgery. VO Although his first redo operation by Dr Patel appeared to be successful, our expert says, that much more extensive investigation of Hennie’s condition should have been done, before making the decision to re-operate…. The risk of complications increased exponentially, every time he went back into theatre. Hennie It’s not nice to feel yourself fading away because my whole life is destroyed. I will never be the same again, never. Nobody can fix that nerve! V/O Hennie believes Dr Patel damaged his vagus nerve during one of the operations… An allegation she vehemently disputes, saying that the nerve damage stemmed from previous procedures, before he consulted with her. Prof Becker Claire: What is a vagus nerve? Prof: It’s a thick white nerve that you can see and especially with laparoscopic surgery very visible. Claire: what then happens if that vagus nerve is severed. How would that affect a person going forward? Prof: Ja, you see the Vagus nerve has multiple functions in the abdomen. If the vagus nerve is cut, then the stomach becomes paralysed. Marcia This kid's gone through hell. He went through hell because of her. V/O Bjorn and Marcia Trumplemann’s son, Reece, is also dealing with long term damage. During his second surgery with Dr Patel, his vagus nerve was severed. Marcia It turned out that his stomach was actually sitting on his hip, it was completely bloated and full of food. Food wasn’t passing through anymore… Claire: What did they explain that would mean to Reese? Marcia; Life-long complications. Lifelong. VO ROR Reece Dr Patel denies that Reece’s vagus nerve was damaged, but these images and medical reports suggest otherwise. Our expert says vagus nerve damage is an unacceptable complication, and “can only occur with negligent conduct”. Dr Patel also insists that the family did not struggle to arrange follow-up appointments after Reece’s surgery, and claims they were happy with his treatment. She says the Trumplemann’s were banned from Arwyp Medical Centre, after threatening to sue the hospital. But Arwyp told us this is not true. Marsha This doctor sucked us so deep in that I allowed her to operate multiple times on him because I believed her… [PAUSE] LINK timeline Our investigation goes back as far as 2018 when Dr Soraya Patel gained rights to practise at Netcare Sunward Hospital. V/O Not long after she started at Sunward Park, on Joburg’s East Rand, fellow surgeons said they’d witnessed Dr Patel conducting “unusually lengthy” operations on patients, while others experienced serious post-surgical complications. V/O Doctors told hospital management and the Health Professions Council of South Africa – or HPCSA – that some of Dr Patel’s patients had died… and made other claims of alleged malpractice. They believed Dr Patel had also performed numerous unnecessary surgeries. Netcare management requested a peer review but she declined… Instead she sued the doctors and hospital manager. None of these doctors would speak on camera, with some saying they fear for their lives. V/O Dr Patel believes this was a baseless complaint, motivated by professional jealousy, considering that she was a young, successful female surgeon with a flourishing practice at that time. Dr Patel says she refused to participate in the requested peer review because she wasn’t provided with enough information about the complaints. She insists she has an excellent track record, with mortality rates that are consistent with averages for high-risk surgery. LINK Netcare banned her from all their hospitals but she just moved 22kms down the road to Arwyp Medical Centre. Business as usual. V/O ROR Arwyp And she has been practising here for almost six years. Arwyp management told us they weren’t aware of any complaints against Dr Patel raised by a patient, or of any excessively long surgical procedures performed by her. LINK Arwyp Medical Centre told us that all their doctors are properly vetted and are in good standing with the HPCSA…. But how is that possible with such a trail of cases behind Dr Patel? VO HPCSA Despite numerous concerns about Dr Patel’s treatment of patients over the last six years, not one judgement against her appears on the HPCSA’s website. VO Kwena Mabasa is their Head of Complaints Handling and Investigation. HPCSA Head: Complaints handling and Investigation Claire: How many complaints have been brought to the HPCSA Against Dr Patel? Do we know? Kwena: Based on our register of record there are 17 complaints that we would have received in total. Claire: Is that not worrying? Kwena: Not necessarily, because, remember we can receive 17 complaints and 10 of those are issues related to I need my statement of account. V/O But we know that one of those 17 complaints was from that group of surgeons working alongside Dr Patel at Sunward Park in 2019, … and their concerns had nothing to do with outstanding statements. HPCSA Head: Complaints handling and Investigation Kwena Mabasa Claire: They had very serious allegations against her; botched operations, deaths of patients, procedures that they felt were unnecessary… Kwena: There was no evidence in terms of the clinical records that were provided that the patients were mismanaged by Dr Patel… V/O The surgeons disagree. Even though they submitted a detailed complaint in April 2019, they never heard from the HPCSA again… HPCSA Head: Complaints handling and Investigation Claire: So, in the meantime, with all of these complaints she’s registered and still practising? Kwena: She is registered and she is practising but we are doing what we are mandated to do. We just cannot disclose the cases obviously now. V/O While the HPCSA continues their investigations, Dr Patel has again opted for legal retaliation. HPCSA Head: Complaints handling and Investigation Kwena Mabasa Claire: We understand that Dr Patel did sue HPCSA, correct? Kwena: Uhm, we can confirm our litigation office received the papers. As to what is contained in the papers, at this point, that cannot be disclosed. V/O The very day after this interview, the surgeons suddenly received this letter… confirming the outcome of a meeting held in September 2021… when the HPCSA apparently found no evidence that Patel should be formally investigated. Apparently the 3-year delay in sending this communication was due to a backlog… [PAUSE] VO Dr Patel maintains that she does not perform unnecessary or unusually long surgeries and says, her patients neither require frequent “re-dos” nor remain in high care longer than needed. VO ROR Ghoor Ultimately, her main counterclaim is that in most cases, she was “not the one holding the knife”. She claims that her partner in practice, Professor Faizulla Ghoor was the primary surgeon, and she was merely the assistant. But it’s Dr Patel’s name that appears on almost every record and bill… and most of the patients say they hardly met Professor Ghoor, and were not aware that he would be doing the surgery. Despite a flurry of lawyer’s letters, we got no clear answer from Prof Ghoor. [PAUSE] LINK We’ve heard the stories of what seemed to be a caring and capable doctor that became cold and quite malicious when things started to go wrong. And many of her patients are still left with very few answers. V/O On the 2nd of August, Arwyp Medical Centre suspended Dr Patel in light of the serious nature of the allegations levelled against her… But for these former patients it brings little comfort as their suffering is still a daily reality. Hennie I don't want to live anymore. I’d rather die instead of having this feeling the whole time. Christo I've got memory loss due to all the anaesthesia and also the morphine… And, I mean, this has put my whole life on hold basically. V/O But these people represent a fraction of the stories we’ve heard. And who knows how many others are suffering in silence? Elzette It’s just sad and infuriating that she’s messed up so many people’s lives. How many people still has to go through this? How many people still has to suffer? END END PART 4 ROR Since we first asked Dr Patel for an interview in July, we’ve received 12 letters from her lawyers. The last one arrived at 5PM on Friday. 2-6 Dr Patel insists that we haven’t provided enough detail for her to respond fully to our questions. 7-9 She reiterates that she has no pattern of frequent high-care admissions, saying that the fact that our case studies complained about their admissions doesn’t mean they didn’t need high care. However, as our story showed, it was Dr Patel’s colleagues at Netcare Sunward Park who reported this apparent pattern: experts who knew that laparoscopic hernia repairs rarely require more than an overnight stay in a ward. 16-17 Dr Patel insists that Prof Ghoor was the primary surgeon in Reece’s second operation – at the family’s own request. She has provided notes from the operation which name Prof Ghoor as the primary surgeon and herself as the assistant. BUT Reece’s medical reports, as well as this pre-authorisation letter from Discovery, name Dr Patel as his doctor. 18-19 Dr Patel continues to insist that our information about Elzette is incorrect and our evidence is poor. She says she can’t respond to our expert’s opinion without more detailed information. This is a photograph that Dr Patel claims is evidence of the hernia repair she performed on Elzette. 23 Dr Patel also provided photographs which she says prove that Asiem caused massive internal damage to himself by eating solid food, and needed emergency surgery. Our expert says all these photos lack identifying information. The expert says that in Asiem’s case, they don’t portray the damage Dr Patel described; and if Asiem had the condition Dr Patel claims he did, he would probably have died immediately. 38-41 We sent Dr Patel the names of three more patients who gave us permission to show their post-surgery photos. Their names and experiences are not included in our story. But she insists that she doesn’t have enough context to comment on them, and claims that Prof Ghoor “held the knife” in every case. Dr Patel has repeatedly accused us of irresponsible and biased journalism, and urged us to cancel our story. Week after week, we have delayed to ensure that our story is fair, balanced and accurate.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): With numerous botched surgeries reported and even some deaths, we ask the question why is the surgeon responsible still allowed to practice.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We were approached by numerous ex-patients of Dr Soraya Patel about botched operations performed on them by the doctor and the devastating effect it has had on their physical and mental health. The investigation also uncovered that in 5 years , the HPCSA has done nothing to stop the doctor after damning evidence was reported.
metadata.Summary: The story of Soraya Patel starts in 2017 at the Glynwood Life hospital where she practiced as a general surgeon in Laparoscopic surgery. Within months fellow surgeons started to raise flags about her questionable practices. She would perform a routine Lap Nissen ( Hernia) operation for 11 hours. A procedure that normally takes between 27 - 45 minutes. Her patients would be gravely ill post-op an many spent up to a month in high care. It was suggested that she was put under supervision but she declined. She was barred from ever working at a Life Hospital again. She sued the 4 surgeons that reported her. The case was heard in the high court and the judge ruled in favour of the surgeons with cost. She was then granted admission rights to the Netcare Sunward Park hospital. Surgeons at Sunward raised flags with the Hospital Manager Dr Annemarie Richter about Patel's ethical conduct. Despite that Dr Richter continued to give her admission rights to practice. To this day Netcare Group continues their support of Patel's admission rights. The Association of Surgeons was contacted for advice. The suggested peer review but she refused claiming that she was being bullied by a bunch of men. The HPCSA was approached. Patel started sending threatening letters to one of the concerned surgeons, she followed him home one evening and sat watching him from her vehicle when he entered his home. It left the doctor , traumatised and vulnerable. There were numerous reports from staff members who had been offered money. There were complaints from staff that she altered prescriptions - photos were taken by staff. Drains were incorrectly connected but Patel blamed staff. She also removed ICU files. Hospital security had to retrieve the files but some of them had already been altered. Patel also allowed her colleague Prof Ghoor to perform surgeries on patients without the patient knowledge or consent. The doctors also reported her disrespect for the Hypocratic Oath. We have obtained a list of patients deceased after Patel performed surgery. Eventually she was barred from practicing at any Netcare Facility in SA. Patel took legal action agains the doctors that reported her. They are unable and not willing to speak to CB as the case is still pending. Patel then gained admission rights from a private clinic in Kempton Park called Arwyp. She was given admission by the very same person that had her barred from Netcare - Zakeriah Esterhuizen. He moved from Sunward to Arwyp. It is at Arwyp that she performed many questionable surgeries on our case studies.
